body:
Source: GitHub issue #790 (bug, P3-low, area:tickets). Re-verified on main @ b4cff43c: `packages/ticket-sync/lib/providers/github.mjs:49` fails closed on a possibly-truncated fetch with `fetched N issues (hit the limit of 500); narrow the selector or raise --limit`, but `parseFlags` in `bin/ticket-sync.mjs` (lines 31-46) has no `--limit` branch, so `adlc-ticket-sync pull --limit 1000` prints `unknown flag: --limit` and exits 1. `lib/pull.mjs` (lines 106, 116) and `lib/push.mjs` (lines 141, 162) already accept a `limit` option and forward it to `provider.listIssues` only when truthy; the provider defaults to 500 (github.mjs:42). The bin never passes one, so a repo whose selection reaches 500 issues cannot sync at all except by narrowing `select`.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/ticket-sync`: `bin/ticket-sync.mjs` (USAGE, exported `parseFlags`, exported `syncFlow`, `main` dispatching pull/push/sync/doctor), `lib/pull.mjs`, `lib/push.mjs`, `lib/providers/github.mjs` (gh-backed provider, `selectorArgs` puts `--limit` into gh's argv), `lib/gh.mjs` (`makeGhRunner`, spawns `gh` from PATH). Tests: `npm test -w packages/ticket-sync` from the worktree root. `test/cli.test.mjs` pins parseFlags for the existing flags and may gain nothing; `test/github.test.mjs` pins the provider's truncation behaviour and is a rail. `packages/cli` routes `adlc ticket <pull|push|sync|doctor>` here with argv passed through; nothing in `packages/cli` lists these flags and it is out of scope.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. ONE exported pure validator, `parseLimit(raw)`, in a new `packages/ticket-sync/lib/limit.mjs`. It accepts only a decimal string matching `^[1-9][0-9]*$` whose Number is a safe integer, returning `{ ok: true, value }`. Anything else returns `{ ok: false, error }` with `error` exactly `invalid --limit: <raw> (expected a positive integer)`, except a missing value (undefined, or a next token beginning with `--`), which returns `--limit requires a positive integer value`. No throwing, no coercion (`'1e3'`, `'1.0'`, `' 5'`, `'0x10'` are all invalid).
2. `parseFlags` accepts `--limit <n>` as two argv tokens, consuming the value token. On an invalid or missing value it writes the validator's error plus a newline to stderr and exits 1, writing nothing to stdout, exactly as the unknown-flag branch does. `flags.limit` is undefined when the flag is absent. A repeated `--limit` takes the last valid value.
3. `main` passes `flags.limit` to `pull({ limit })` and `push({ limit })`, including both halves of `sync`. Absent the flag, the calls behave exactly as today (provider default 500).
4. The truncation error text in `lib/providers/github.mjs` is unchanged: it becomes true. Truncation still fails closed at any limit.
5. USAGE lists `[--limit <n>]` with a one-line description. Documentation: add `--limit <n>` where `packages/ticket-sync/README.md` describes the commands' flags, and to the usage line and flag table in `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/ticket-sync.mdx`. There is no `docs/tools/ticket-sync.md`; do not create one.
6. The end-to-end test puts a fake `gh` on PATH that records its argv. The fake must NOT read stdin: this package's runner (`lib/gh.mjs`) uses async `execFile`, which never writes to or closes the child's stdin, so a `cat > /dev/null` drain blocks forever waiting for an EOF that never arrives (measured: the draining shim hangs, the non-draining one returns in ~5 ms). A stdin drain is only correct for callers that pass `input` to spawnSync, where an unread pipe can surface as EPIPE; no ticket-sync call does.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `parseLimit` accepts '1' and '1000'; rejects '0', '-1', '1.5', '1e3', 'abc', '', ' 5', '9007199254740993', and undefined, with the exact messages above. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-sync/test/limit-flag.test.mjs`
- AC2 `node packages/ticket-sync/bin/ticket-sync.mjs pull --limit 0` and `... pull --limit` each exit 1 with the validator's message on stderr and empty stdout. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-sync/test/limit-flag.test.mjs`
- AC3 `parseFlags(['--limit','1000']).limit === 1000`; absent flag leaves it undefined; existing flags unaffected. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-sync/test/limit-flag.test.mjs`
- AC4 Spawning the bin's `pull` against a temp repo with a fake `gh` shows `--limit 1000` in the recorded gh argv when `--limit 1000` is passed, and the provider default when it is not. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-sync/test/limit-flag.test.mjs`
- AC5 `--help` output mentions `--limit`. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-sync/test/limit-flag.test.mjs`
- AC6 Existing suite green. verify: `npm test -w packages/ticket-sync`
- AC7 Docs updated. verify: `grep -c -- "--limit" packages/ticket-sync/README.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/ticket-sync.mdx` (each >= 1)
- AC8 Mutation gate green. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally)

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the default of 500; pagination; any change to pull/push/provider logic; `packages/cli`; other open ticket-sync issues.
title: ticket-sync: add the --limit flag the truncation error tells users to raise
